title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
label: Raven

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Raven (4): 23 November 2005 - 26 September 2006" (in-game dates).

how: Raven's fourth reign in the diary's own history and the one billed on Wrestlepalooza, where he beat Goldberg to keep the belt. It carries on through the pages of July to September 2006: Raven keeps it at Summer Assylum when Shawn Michaels interferes against Paul Burchill, and over Goliath at Heatwave. It ends at Anarchy Rulz on 26 September 2006 in the diary's own history, when Shawn Michaels superkicks Raven in a five-on-five brawl and pins him.

It runs through the July 2006 posts, where he keeps it over Tajiri, Lance Storm, Ultimo Dragon, Nate Hatred and Chris Hero and wins the battle royal for it at Summer Assylum, and ends when Rhino takes it.

lost.source: SOURCES DISAGREE: the text of the shows ends this reign at November To Remember (26 November 2006, the date the same history gives that card's tag-title change); the diary's own title history runs it to 28 February 2007. Both readings are recorded (see the note).

how: Vito Thomaselli's first reign in the diary's own history: he pins The Great Sasuke on F' The Mainstream in November after Chris Daniels' chair shot misses him, and keeps the belt on Revolution when a backslide from Daniels leaves both men's shoulders down. note: SOURCES DISAGREE: the diary's own International All Action Championship history lists Vito Thomaselli as champion until 28 February 2007 and names no other holder; the text of the shows has Christopher Daniels take the belt from him at November To Remember (Friday, week 4, November, dated 26 November 2006 by the same history's tag-title entries). Both readings are recorded; the end date follows the text, where the belt changes hands.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
label: Sabu

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Sabu (5): 29 December 2006 - 29 February 2006" (in-game dates; the end as the history prints it is not a calendar date).

lost.source: The text of the shows has Raven beat Sabu on Blood, Sweat and Beers, the show after Living Dangerously; the diary's own title history prints the date as "29 February 2007", which is not a calendar date, so the end is filed at month precision.

how: Sabu's reign in the diary's own history: he wins the belt at Masters Of Pain from Raven with a Triple Jump Moonsault after Zakk Wylde punches the champion, is jumped by Cactus Jack backstage on Blood, Sweat and Beers, keeps the belt over Cactus Jack at Got Blood? with a modified Northern Lights Suplex and the Triple Jump Moonsault, and in February 2007 faces the challenge of Steve Austin, who saved him from Cactus Jack after the match. At Living Dangerously he keeps the belt over Steve Austin with an Atomic Arabian Skullcrusher through a table, and Raven then hits him with an Evenflow DDT; the next night on Blood, Sweat and Beers Raven beats him for the belt with Paul Burchill's and Goliath's help.
note: The diary's own title history prints this reign's end as "29 February 2007" (and its start line prints the year 2006 for the end), which is not a calendar date; the text places the loss on Blood, Sweat and Beers, the show after Living Dangerously, so the end is filed at month precision (February 2007).

note: The diary's own history dates the win 4 December 2006 and the loss 6 February 2007; the text places them on the debut Blood, Sweat and Beers (Saturday, week 1, December) and on Blood, Sweat and Beers (Saturday, week 1, February).

note: The diary's own history dates the end of this reign 28 February 2007; the text places the loss at Living Dangerously (Friday, week 4, February).

how: Christopher Daniels's reign in the diary's own text: he hangs from the belt's harness after the ladder collapses at November To Remember and drops to the floor with the belt in the Stairway To Hell Match with Vito and Super Crazy, keeps it through December (a no contest with Jushin Lyger on Blood, Sweat and Beers when Michael Shane interferes), beats Michael Shane at Got Blood? with Angel's Wings, and is still champion in February 2007, when his Revolution defence against CM Punk ends in a no contest. At Living Dangerously, in the Triangle Match with Michael Shane and CM Punk, Raven hits him with a chair as he climbs to the top rope and Punk pins him for the belt.
note: SOURCES DISAGREE: the diary's own International All Action Championship history names no holder between Vito Thomaselli's win on 5 November 2006 and CM Punk's on 28 February 2007, but the text of the shows has Christopher Daniels hold the belt in between, from November To Remember until Living Dangerously, where Punk beats him for it, the date the history gives for Punk's win. Both readings are recorded; the reign's dates follow the text.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
label: Raven

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Raven (6): 29 February 2007 - 1 October 2007" (in-game dates; 29 February 2007 is not a calendar date, so the win is filed at month precision, and the text puts it on Blood, Sweat and Beers, the show after Living Dangerously).

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the loss is the Monday Revolution of October's first week (PDF p.1448).

how: Raven's sixth reign in the diary's own history: he beats Sabu on the last Blood, Sweat and Beers of February 2007 with an Evenflow DDT after Paul Burchill hits Sabu in the face with the Television Title and Goliath knocks him off the ropes, re-forms the Nest by throwing Charlie Pag and Stephanie Mcintosh through ringside tables, keeps the belt against Shane Douglas at Baptism Of Fire on 29 March 2007 (with CM Punk's interference and three Evenflow DDTs, the last on a chair), which gives him Douglas's powers as commissioner, and is still champion when the pages of April 2007 end. At Cyberslam he keeps the belt over Rhino in the Steel Cage Match when Paul Burchill, the special referee, counts fast and calls a submission Rhino never gave, and Burchill then turns on him with a C-4; at Hardcore Heaven, in a match that is not for the title, he beats Burchill after CM Punk threatens to throw Kelly Thomaselli off the stage, and he is still champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end, with Owen Hart booked to challenge him at Wrestlepalooza and Bret Hart in a Triangle Match for the belt. At Wrestlepalooza Raven keeps the belt in the elimination Triangle Match when Bret and Owen Hart quarrel, Owen makes Bret tap to the Ankle Lock, and Raven hits Owen with the Raven Effect onto a chair; the giant in black, the mystery signing Mark Calaway, Chokeslams him, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers Paul Heyman forces him into a non-title match with Vito Thomaselli, where Calaway's Chokeslam lets Vito pin him. At Summer Assylum he keeps the belt over Calaway when Rhino Gores Calaway and Raven covers, and he is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with Vito Thomaselli asking Paul Heyman for the title match at Heatwave. At Heatwave in August 2007, in the Barbed Wire Cage Match Raven names, Vito Thomaselli beats him (Burchill's Corkscrew Cross Body from the top of the cage, then the Vito Driver) and is presented with the belt, but CM Punk hits Burchill with the International All Action belt and Vito with a GTS and carries the belt to Raven; on Blood, Sweat and Beers Raven reads out clause 17.2a of the contract (interference from any party voids any title change) and says the belt still belongs to him and that Vito was never champion. Rhino wins the first Buck Stops Here Match at Heatwave to become number one contender and is booked against Raven at Anarchy Rulz; Raven is still champion when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Raven beats Rhino with Mark Calaway's help (Calaway's Elevated Powerbomb and Chokeslam, and Raven pins Rhino) and is then chokeslammed by Calaway. On Revolution on 1 October 2007 Owen Hart makes him tap to the Sharpshooter after Chris Jericho's chair shot: the reign ends there.
note: The diary's own history gives this reign's start as "29 February 2007", which is not a calendar date, so the win is filed at month precision (the text places it the night after Living Dangerously); the history's end of 1 October 2007 is the Revolution of October's first week (PDF p.1448), where Owen Hart makes Raven tap.

note: The diary's own history dates the win 28 February 2007 and the loss 22 March 2007; the text places them at Living Dangerously (Friday, week 4, February) and on Blood, Sweat and Beers (Saturday, week 3, March).

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Television Championship, listed as "Bret Hart (2): 22 March 2007 - 15 April 2007" (in-game dates).

note: The diary's own history dates the win 22 March 2007 and the loss 15 April 2007; the text places them on Blood, Sweat and Beers (Saturday, week 3, March) and on Blood, Sweat and Beers (Saturday, week 2, April).

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-television
label: Chris Jericho

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Television Championship, listed as "Chris Jericho (4): 15 April 2007 - 24 April 2007" (in-game dates).

how: Chris Jericho's fourth Television reign in the diary's own history: he pins Bret Hart in the Triangle Match with Christian on Blood, Sweat and Beers in the second week of April after Christian clotheslines the champion off the Sharpshooter; Rob Van Dam is booked to challenge him for the belt at Cyberslam. At Cyberslam he defends against Rob Van Dam in the Lumberjack Match; Shawn Michaels's Superkick off the ropes as he springboards for a Lionsault, while Christian is held at ringside, sets up Van Dam's Five Star Frog Splash, and Van Dam pins him for the belt.
note: The diary's own history dates the win 15 April 2007 and the loss 24 April 2007; the text places the loss at Cyberslam (Friday, week 4, April), the card the history dates 24 April 2007 for Rob Van Dam's win.

label: The Iron Saints (Salvatore and Brandon Thomaselli)

how: The Iron Saints' reign in the diary's own history: Salvatore and Brandon Thomaselli cash in their title shot at Living Dangerously and beat the Whole F**kin' Show for the belts with a Spike Powerbomb on Shawn Michaels after Rob Van Dam steps off the apron, keep them against Crouching Lyger Hidden Dragon on Blood, Sweat and Beers with the Canadian Connection's interference, and lose them at Baptism Of Fire in the first Halflife Handicap match.
note: The diary's own history dates the win 28 February 2007 and the loss 29 March 2007; the text places them at Living Dangerously (Friday, week 4, February) and at Baptism Of Fire (Friday, week 4, March).

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
label: The Whole F**kin' Show (Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "The Whole F**kin' Show (2): 29 March 2007 - 26 October 2007" (in-game dates).

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the loss is the Three Way Dance at Guilty As Charged (PDF p.1545).

how: The Whole F**kin' Show's second reign in the diary's own history: Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels beat the Iron Saints at Baptism Of Fire in the first Halflife Handicap match, with Michaels's Sweet Chin Music and a Five Star Frog Splash on Salvatore, and are the champions when the pages of April 2007 end, with Rob Van Dam set to defend them while challenging Chris Jericho at Cyberslam. At Cyberslam they keep the belts over Los Increibles in the Ladder Match when Rob Van Dam pulls them down; at Hardcore Heaven Shawn Michaels, bloodied and alone while Van Dam helps Traci, keeps them over the Canadian Connection with a third Sweet Chin Music on Christian; the champions quarrel through June but are still champions when the pages of June 2007's second week end. At Wrestlepalooza they keep the belts over the Hardcore Innovators when Michaels's Diving Elbow and Van Dam's Five Star Frog Splash win simultaneous covers; the Dudley Boyz win the number one contendership on Blood, Sweat and Beers and, at Summer Assylum, the Whole F**kin' Show beat them in the Tables Match with Michaels's Sweet Chin Music through a table on D-Von; they are still champions when the pages of August 2007's first week end. After Heatwave the Whole F**kin' Show attack the new Dudleyville Hardcore Tag Team Champions, the Hardcore Innovators; in September they keep the belts over the Dudley Boyz on Revolution with simultaneous finishers, accept the Innovators' challenge for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz, quarrel after Shawn Michaels is caught covering Traci, and are still champions when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 they lose the Champions versus Champions match by a no contest after the Dudley Family run in; in October the partners quarrel over the stipulation for the Three Way Dance until Paul Heyman books ladders, chairs, canes and flaming tables, and at Guilty As Charged Shawn Michaels's Super Kick takes Rob Van Dam out of the air and Bubba Ray pins him: the reign ends there.
note: The diary's own history dates the win 29 March 2007 and the loss 26 October 2007, Guilty As Charged (PDF p.1545), where the Dudley Boyz pin Rob Van Dam after Shawn Michaels's Super Kick.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
label: CM Punk

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW International All Action Championship, listed as "CM Punk: 28 February 2007 - 29 September 2007" (in-game dates); the text of the shows agrees with that date for the win.

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date (a day after the date of the show, Friday, week 4, September 2007), and the text agrees: the loss is the International All Action Championship Match at Anarchy Rulz (PDF p.1419).

how: CM Punk's first reign in the diary's own history: he pins Christopher Daniels in the Triangle Match with Michael Shane at Living Dangerously after Raven hits Daniels with a chair, pins Daniels again with a low blow on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and attacks Lance Storm, who won an International All Action title shot in the Stairway To Hell match at Baptism Of Fire, and is still champion when the pages of April 2007 end. At Cyberslam he keeps the belt over Lance Storm in the No Way Out Match with a GTS, and at Hardcore Heaven he keeps it over Storm again with a GTS after Monsters Inc chokeslam Storm onto Abyss's knee; he is still champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end. On Revolution in June Punk knocks out Paul Burchill and Shane Douglas with the belt, and at Wrestlepalooza Vito Thomaselli turns on him with a chair; the belt is not defended in this range, and he is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, having been powerbombed through a table by Vito at Summer Assylum. At Heatwave in August 2007 Punk hits Burchill with the belt and the new World Heavyweight Champion with a GTS; in September he defends it for the first time in months and keeps it over Lance Storm (a GTS), over Big Sasuke Cool (a GTS after Monsters Inc.'s interference) and over Eddie Guerrero (a GTS), and he is still champion when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end, with Vito Thomaselli booked against him at Anarchy Rulz. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Vito Thomaselli pins him with a Crucifix Roll-Up after a Springboard Somersault Plancha takes down Monsters Inc.: the reign ends there.
note: The diary's own history dates the win 28 February 2007 and the loss 29 September 2007, Anarchy Rulz (PDF p.1419), where Vito Thomaselli pins Punk with a Crucifix Roll-Up. The history names no holder between Vito Thomaselli and CM Punk, while the text of the shows has Christopher Daniels hold the belt in between (see his reign).

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-television
label: Rob Van Dam

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Television Championship, listed as "Rob Van Dam (3): 24 April 2007 - 29 May 2007" (in-game dates); the text of the shows puts the win at Cyberslam and the loss at Hardcore Heaven, the dates the history gives for those cards.

how: Rob Van Dam's third Television reign in the diary's own history: he beats Chris Jericho at Cyberslam in the Lumberjack Match, when Shawn Michaels Superkicks Jericho off the ropes while Christian is held at ringside and a Five Star Frog Splash makes the pin; AJ Styles's debut in May and Van Dam's jealousy over Traci set him against Michaels, and at Hardcore Heaven AJ Styles, helped by the Canadian Connection's hockey sticks while Michaels is not at ringside, pins him with the Styles Clash for the belt.
note: The diary's own history dates the win 24 April 2007 and the loss 29 May 2007; the text places them at Cyberslam (Friday, week 4, April) and at Hardcore Heaven (Friday, week 4, May), whose date, 29 May 2007, Joel Gertner's rhyme names as the day of the show.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-television
label: AJ Styles

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Television Championship, listed as "AJ Styles: 29 May 2007 - 28 September 2007" (in-game dates); the text of the shows agrees with the date for the win.

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the loss is the World Television Championship Match at Anarchy Rulz (PDF p.1413).

how: AJ Styles's first Television reign in the diary's own history: he debuts on Blood, Sweat and Beers in May 2007, turns on Rob Van Dam and Traci with the Canadian Connection and wins the belt at Hardcore Heaven; he beats Rey Mysterio Jr. with a low blow and a small package, takes a second defence on Revolution in June with an illegal use of the ropes, loses a non-title match to Juventud Guerrera, and is still champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end. On Revolution in June he beats Juventud Guerrera with a low blow and the Styles Clash, and at Wrestlepalooza he keeps the belt over Guerrera when Styles pushes Guerrera's foot off the rope before the Styles Clash is counted and Jim Molineaux does not see it; at Summer Assylum he keeps it again when Francine pretends to turn on Guerrera and Christopher Daniels, aligned with Styles, hits Guerrera with the belt; he is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with Guerrera's challenge for Heatwave on 28 August unanswered and Ultimo Dragon billed against him. At Heatwave in August 2007, in the Stairway To Hell Match, Styles keeps the belt over Juventud Guerrera, who loses his mask: it hangs from one hook and the belt from the other; on Blood, Sweat and Beers in September he keeps it again, beating Jerry Lynn with a roll-up after pointing at the entrance-way to make Lynn look for Kurt Angle; he is still champion when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end, with Ultimo Dragon booked against him at Anarchy Rulz. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Ultimo Dragon pins him with an Asai DDT after Styles drags Francine into the ring and Dragon cuts off a Styles Clash with an elbow: the reign ends there.
note: The diary's own history dates the win 29 May 2007 and the loss 28 September 2007, Anarchy Rulz (PDF p.1413), where Ultimo Dragon pins Styles with the Asai DDT.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-dudleyville-hardcore-tag-team
label: The Dudley Boyz (Bubba Ray and D-Von)

won.source: Declared by the Dudleyz themselves on Blood, Sweat and Beers the night after Summer Assylum, July 2007: the old World Tag Team Championships, renamed the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, with no match; the diary's own title history (PDF p.8) lists the belt as "Dudley Boyz: 28 July 2007 - 24 August 2007 (Dudley Boyz debut titles on Blood, Sweat & Beers)" (in-game dates).

lost.source: The diary's own title history (PDF p.8) gives this date; the belt is lost in the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship Match at Heatwave (Friday, week 4, August 2007).

how: The Dudley Boyz's only reign in this range: they say on Blood, Sweat and Beers that the belts are the old World Tag Team Championships from when they dominated the division and that these are now the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, with the second generation of Dudleyz at their side; they make the first defence on Revolution in August, beating the bWo with a 3D on Hollywood Nova after Chessman and Oz hit the bWo with the belts, beat Balls & Axl with a 3D on Axl on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and are challenged by the Hardcore Innovators for Heatwave and by Los Guerreros. In August 2007 they keep the belts over Los Guerreros, the Samoan Gangstas and the Briscoe Boys, with their relatives' help; the Hardcore Innovators cane them after the last of these and walk off with the belts, and at Heatwave Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer win the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship Match, putting D-Von through a table with a Double DDT: the reign ends there.
note: The belt is the Dudleyz's own, made and named by them on screen; no match is wrestled for it. The diary's own title history (PDF p.8) lists it and dates this reign 28 July 2007 (the Saturday show the night after Summer Assylum) to 24 August 2007, Heatwave (Friday, week 4, August 2007), where the Hardcore Innovators win the belts.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-dudleyville-hardcore-tag-team
label: The Hardcore Innovators (Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer)

won.source: Won from the Dudley Boyz in the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship Match at Heatwave (Friday, week 4, August 2007), PDF p.1279: "We have new champions! We have new champions!"; the diary's own title history (PDF p.8) lists the belt as "Hardcore Innovators (Cactus Jack & Tommy Dreamer: 24 August 2007 - 26 October 2007" (in-game dates).

lost.source: The diary's own title history (PDF p.8) gives this date, and the text agrees: the belts are lost in the Three Way Dance at Guilty As Charged (PDF p.1545).

how: Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer beat the Dudley Boyz for the belts at Heatwave: the Innovators cane the second generation of Dudleyz on the outside, Cactus Jack's Double Arm DDT catches Bubba Ray as he rebounds, Dreamer rakes D-Von's eye, and the two put D-Von through a table with a Double DDT before Cactus covers (1...2...3). Joey Styles says the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship has become the ECW Hardcore Championship, the diary's later previews call the belts the (newly rechristened) ECW Hardcore Tag Team Championship, and the Whole F**kin' Show attack the new champions after the match. In September, with Beulah McGillicutty at their side, the Innovators ask the World Tag Team Champions for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz to crown the Undisputed Tag Team Champions; they are still the holders when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 the Innovators lose the Champions versus Champions match by a no contest when the Dudley Family run in; in October, with Beulah McGillicutty, they ask Paul Heyman for a Singapore Cane Match, and at Guilty As Charged they are eliminated in the Three Way Dance (Bubba Ray pins Tommy Dreamer, then Cactus Jack): the reign ends there, 26 October 2007, though they leave the arena with all four belts and take them again from ringside after beating the second generation of Dudleyz on Blood, Sweat and Beers.
note: The belt is the Dudleyz's own, made and named by them on screen and won from them here. The diary's own title history (PDF p.8) lists it and dates this reign 24 August 2007 (Heatwave) to 26 October 2007 (Guilty As Charged). The diary's text calls the belts the ECW Hardcore Tag Team Championship after this match; the title's own page keeps the name the Dudleyz gave it.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
label: Owen Hart

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Owen Hart: 1 October 2007 - 26 October 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Revolution, Monday, week 1, October 2007, PDF p.1448: "WE HAVE A NEW CHAMPION! WE HAVE A NEW CHAMPION!"

how: Owen Hart beats Raven on Revolution, the first televised defence of the title since February: he reverses Raven's Evenflow DDT into a Northern Lights Suplex, clears The Nest with a chair, and when Chris Jericho slips in and hits Raven with a chair, locks in the Sharpshooter and Raven taps; referee John Finnegan hands him the belt and Owen weeps. Jericho challenges him on Blood, Sweat and Beers and Paul Heyman books a Number One Contender's Match; Owen is the special guest referee in the tag match of Mark Calaway and Rhino against Raven and Jericho, refuses to count Raven's pin, and saves Jericho from The Nest in the cage match. He has announced that he will retire after Guilty As Charged, and his last match there is the 30-minute Ultimate Submission Match against Jericho: Hart's Sharpshooter wins the first fall, Jericho's Liontamer the second, and Jericho's Sharpshooter the third, and with seconds left Hart reverses a Figure Four into a Sharpshooter; Jericho taps at 30:00 and John Finnegan rules that the tap came after the time limit, so Jericho is declared the champion and Hart hands him the belt.
note: The history's dates (1 October and 26 October 2007) are the ones filed, and the text agrees: Revolution is a Monday show (1 October 2007 was a Monday) and Guilty As Charged is dated 'the 26th day of October'.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
label: Chris Jericho

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Chris Jericho (2): 26 October 2007 (10:54 pm) - 26 October 2007 (11:02 pm)" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1561: "Your winner and NEW Extreme Championship Wrestling World Heavyweight Champion... Chris Jericho!"

how: Jericho is declared champion at the end of the Ultimate Submission Match when referee John Finnegan rules that his tap came after the time limit; Owen Hart passes him the belt and raises his hand and the two hug. Raven slides in, boots Hart out of the ring and hits Jericho with a Raven Effect, then uses the Commissioner's right to book one match of his own at each pay-per-view: Raven versus Chris Jericho for the World Heavyweight Title; Raven covers Jericho and Finnegan counts three.
note: The history times the reign to the minute, 10:54 pm to 11:02 pm on 26 October 2007, so it lasts eight minutes (days: 0). The diary has the Commissioner's right to book a pay-per-view match stand as legitimate (p.1569, Don Callis: 'Raven's controversial reclaiming... was legitimate under promotional guidelines').

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
label: Raven

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Raven (7): 26 October 2007 - 30 November 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1562: "Your winner and new seven-time ECW World Heavyweight Champion... Raven!"

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the loss is the Loser Leaves ECW Match at November To Remember XV (PDF p.1721).

how: Raven pins Jericho with the Commissioner's match and leaves with the belt as fans throw rubbish into the ring. On Blood, Sweat and Beers Don Callis apologises on the company's behalf and says that the win was legitimate under the promotional guidelines; the company's owner then returns, strips Raven of his powers as Commissioner, gives sole booking power to Paul Heyman and books Raven's defence at November To Remember XV against Paul Burchill: 'The natural order has been restored.' Raven is still the champion when the pages of October 2007 end. In November 2007 Paul Heyman, back in power, tells Raven on Revolution that nobody in the arena is comfortable seeing him as the champion and that Paul Burchill will beat him at November To Remember; Burchill, Vito Thomaselli and Chris Jericho beat members of Raven's Nest on Revolution and on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and on the third Blood, Sweat and Beers Heyman makes the title match a Loser Leaves ECW Match, with anyone outside it who touches either man to be fired and barred from signing with the Federation, and says that the man who stays will be the Undisputed ECW World Heavyweight Champion. Raven is still the champion when the diary's preview of the card ends. Raven loses the Loser Leaves ECW Match to Paul Burchill at November To Remember XV (PDF p.1721) after a contest the diary rates A*: Burchill's C-4 from the top rope and a Shooting Star Press end the reign, and Raven, kneeling in the aisle, is out of ECW (the diary's next preview: 'Never again will Raven be seen in an ECW ring').
note: The history ends this reign on 30 November 2007, and the text agrees: the loss is the Loser Leaves ECW Match at November To Remember XV (Friday, week 4, November 2007, PDF p.1721); the history's date is the one filed.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-television
label: Ultimo Dragon

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Television Championship, listed as "Ultimo Dragon (2): 28 September 2007 - 26 October 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Anarchy Rulz, PDF p.1413: "We have a new World Teelevision Champion!"

how: Ultimo Dragon beats AJ Styles at Anarchy Rulz: Styles powerbombs him to the concrete, then drags Francine into the ring for a Styles Clash, Dragon cuts him off with an elbow, flips over Styles's shoulders and hits the Asai DDT, and Francine presents him the belt and kisses him. He keeps it over Big Sasuke Cool (an Asai DDT) on Blood, Sweat and Beers, over Rey Mysterio Jr. on the second Revolution of October (an Asai DDT after Styles misses a springboard clothesline) and in a non-title match against Mysterio on the fourth (a Dragon Suplex after Francine distracts him), and accepts Styles's challenge, made by Francine, for Guilty As Charged. There the four-way Stairway To Hell Match ends his reign when Styles pulls the belt from the strap.
note: The history's dates (28 September and 26 October 2007) are the ones filed; the text of Anarchy Rulz and Guilty As Charged agrees.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-television
label: AJ Styles

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Television Championship, listed as "AJ Styles (2): 26 October 2007 - 26 November 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, the Stairway To Hell Match, PDF p.1548

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the loss is the television title rematch on Revolution, Monday, week 4, November 2007 (PDF p.1662).

how: Styles wins the four-way Stairway To Hell Match against Christopher Daniels, Rey Mysterio Jr. and the champion Ultimo Dragon: hanging from the strap that holds the belt alongside Dragon, he shifts his hands onto the belt and crashes to the canvas with it. Juventud Guerrera then runs in with a chair and hits all four men, signalling that he is coming for the belt. On Blood, Sweat and Beers on the first Saturday of November 2007 Styles keeps the title by pinning Juventud Guerrera with a Styles Clash while Guerrera's foot is on the rope and the referee misses it; Guerrera pulls him back through the ropes for a Juvi Driver, and Rey Mysterio Jr., Christopher Daniels and Ultimo Dragon run in and beat Guerrera down until Francine dives on top of him. Styles beats Mysterio with a Styles Clash on Revolution the following Monday, and on Revolution on the last Monday of the month Guerrera pins him in the rematch and wins the title: the reign ends there.
note: The history ends this reign on 26 November 2007, and the text agrees: the loss is the television title rematch on Revolution, Monday, week 4, November 2007 (PDF p.1662), the show before November To Remember XV; the history's date is the one filed.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
label: Vito Thomaselli

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW International All Action Championship, listed as "Vito Thomaselli (2): 29 September 2007 - 26 October 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Anarchy Rulz, PDF p.1419: "He did it! He just outsmarted Punk!"

how: Vito Thomaselli beats CM Punk at Anarchy Rulz with a Crucifix Roll-Up after a Springboard Somersault Plancha takes down Monsters Inc., and Punk beats him down afterwards. He keeps it over Jushin Lyger with the Vito Driver on Revolution, and the feud turns personal: Punk hits him with a GTS, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers Vito answers by forcing beer and a cigarette on the straight-edge Punk. At Guilty As Charged, in the Last Man Standing Match, Punk and Monsters Inc. beat him down with GTSs, chair shots and Abyss's Black Hole Slam until referee Jim Molineaux stops the match and Bob Artese announces Punk the new champion.
note: The history dates the win 29 September 2007, a day after the show's date (the show is filed under Friday, week 4, September 2007); the history's dates are the ones filed.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
label: CM Punk

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW International All Action Championship, listed as "CM Punk (2): 26 October 2007 - 3 November 2007 (stripped of title)" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1555: "Your winner and NEW ECW International All Action Champion..."

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees that the belt is taken from Punk by security guards on Revolution, Monday, week 1, November 2007 (PDF p.1583).

how: Punk wins the Last Man Standing Match when referee Jim Molineaux stops it and keeps the belt on Blood, Sweat and Beers over Lance Storm with a GTS after eight minutes. On Revolution on the first Monday of November 2007 Paul Heyman has about fifteen security guards strip Punk of the belt ('That International All Action Title... it ain't yours anymore'), and starts a tournament for it among 'hard working, respectful talent': the reign ends there.
note: The history ends this reign on 3 November 2007 with the title stripped (it then lists the title vacant, 'to be awarded to winner of championship tournament'); the text agrees that Paul Heyman strips the belt on Revolution, Monday, week 1, November 2007 (PDF p.1583) and starts the International All Action Title Tournament, whose final is on the card of November To Remember XV; the history's date is the one filed.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
label: The Dudley Boyz (Bubba Ray and D-Von)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "Dudley Boyz (9): 26 October 2007 - 4 November 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1545: "The Dudley Boyz are the new unified tag champs..."

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date; the pages of November 2007 do not show the loss, and the diary's preview of November To Remember XV (PDF p.1676) bills the Dudley Boyz as the champions.

how: The Dudley Boyz win the Ladders, Chairs, Canes and Flaming Tables Three Way Dance for both sets of tag belts: Bubba Ray eliminates D-Von's opponents in turn, and when Shawn Michaels's Super Kick takes Rob Van Dam out of the air he pins Van Dam. The Hardcore Innovators then leave the arena with the belts, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers the Innovators beat the Second Generation of Dudleyz and take all four belts from ringside again. In November 2007 the Hardcore Innovators still walk to the ring with all four belts, and Bubba Ray and D-Von challenge them for a title match at November To Remember XV; on the third Blood, Sweat and Beers Paul Heyman announces the Undisputed ECW Tag Team belts and a match in which the Dudley Boyz and the Innovators unify the titles, and the diary's preview of the card bills the Dudley Boyz as the champions. At November To Remember XV (PDF pp.1706-1707) the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators, who carry both tag belts, in a weapons match with the Second Generation of Dudleyz and Daizy at ringside (a Superbomb through a table for Beulah McGillicutty, a Dudley Death Drop through a flaming table for Tommy Dreamer, B) and raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles. On Revolution on the first Monday of December they lose the Undisputed belts in a restarted Three Way Dance when Slyk Tayshaun Dudley makes Bubba Ray tap to the Boston Crabs.
note: The history ends this reign on 4 November 2007 and lists the Second Generation of Dudleyz (Big Dick Dudley Jr. and Slyk Tayshaun Dudley) as the champions from then, 'present'; the pages show something else: the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators at November To Remember XV (30 November), are called the first Undisputed ECW Tag Team Champions on the Saturday show and on Revolution, and lose the belts to Slyk and Dick Jr. on Revolution on the first Monday of December (PDF p.1747). The history's date is the one filed; the conflict is stated, not settled.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-dudleyville-hardcore-tag-team
label: The Dudley Boyz (Bubba Ray and D-Von)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW/Dudleyville Hardcore Tag Team Championship, listed as "Dudley Boyz (2): 26 October 2007 - 30 November 2007" (in-game dates; PDF p.8); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1545, the Three Way Dance to unify the tag team championships

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the belt is unified with the World Tag Team Championship in the Undisputed Tag Team Championship Match at November To Remember XV (PDF pp.1706-1707).

how: The Dudley Boyz win the Three Way Dance at Guilty As Charged, which the card bills as the match 'to unify the tag team championships', and take back the Dudleyville belts from the Hardcore Innovators; the Innovators leave with the belts, and retrieve all four again on Blood, Sweat and Beers. In November 2007 Paul Heyman announces the Undisputed ECW Tag Team belts and a match at November To Remember XV in which the Dudley Boyz and the Hardcore Innovators unify the tag titles. At November To Remember XV the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators and raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles; the Dudleyville belts are unified with the World Tag Team belts there, on the date (30 November 2007) the diary's history gives.
note: The history lists this belt separately and gives the reign as running to 30 November 2007, when it is 'unified with the World Tag Team Championship', and the text agrees: the unification is the Undisputed Tag Team Championship Match at November To Remember XV (PDF pp.1706-1707); the World Tag Team history treats the Dudley Boyz as holders of the undisputed titles from 26 October, and each history's date is filed in its own title.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-lioness
label: Alexis Laree

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW Lioness Championship, listed as "Alexis Laree: 28 September 2007 - present (won a Lioness' Den Match to crown the first champion)" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Anarchy Rulz, PDF pp.1420-1421, the Lioness' Den Match

how: Alexis Laree wins the first Lioness' Den Match at Anarchy Rulz against Jazz and Kelly Thomaselli: Jazz kicks out of two Alexis Effects, hits her Fisherman Brainbuster on a chair, and Kelly Thomaselli breaks up the cover and hits Jazz with the chair; Alexis rolls Kelly up and hooks her tights for the three, and Joey Styles calls it 'underhanded'. She keeps the belt over Daizy Dudley on Blood, Sweat and Beers, over Beulah McGillicutty and Traci on Revolution and Blood, Sweat and Beers, and over Jazz at Guilty As Charged, when Nattie Neidhart, the 'anonymous blonde', runs in and the two hit a Double DDT; she is still the champion when the pages of October 2007 end. In November 2007 Jazz and Kelly Thomaselli beat Alexis and Nathalie in a Lioness Pack Match, Alexis jumps Kelly after Kelly beats Nathalie, and on the last Revolution before November To Remember XV Alexis pins Jazz in a non-title match after Nathalie hits Jazz with the belt and the two land a Double DDT onto it; Kelly then clears both with the belt and challenges for the title, and the diary's preview of the card bills Kelly Thomaselli against Alexis, the champion. At November To Remember XV Alexis beats Kelly Thomaselli in the Lioness match (the preview bills it with Alexis as the champion) with an Alexis Effect when Nathalie slides in with the Lioness belt and hits Kelly from behind, then Alexis and Nathalie beat Kelly down until Jazz clears them (C). On Revolution on the first Monday of December she beats Mika Akino with an Alexis Effect (D+) and on the Saturday show again (E+, 5:42); Kong, back 'from APW' with Prince Nana, then flattens her with a bodycheck and a Sit-out Powerbomb. The diary's next preview books Kong and Akino against Alexis and Nathalie in a Lioness Pack Match.
note: The history lists the reign as 'present', so no end date is filed: the diary's record ends with her still the champion.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-television
label: Juventud Guerrera

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Television Championship, listed as "Juventud Guerrera: 26 November 2007 - present" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Revolution, Monday, week 4, November 2007, PDF p.1662: "He did it! He did it! Guerrera has his first ECW Gold!"

how: Juventud Guerrera pins AJ Styles on Revolution in the rematch that Paul Heyman has booked for the show before November To Remember XV: Guerrera hooks Styles for a Juvi Driver, Styles slips over his shoulder, Guerrera hits an Enziguiri and Styles climbs for a corkscrew leg drop, the Spiral Tap, but Guerrera hooks his leg and rolls through into a pin, for his first title in ECW. Ultimo Dragon, the number one contender after a three-way match on Blood, Sweat and Beers, appears at the entrance with Francine, points at her and then at his own waist, and the champion's first defence is the World Television Championship Match against him at November To Remember XV. Juventud Guerrera keeps the title at November To Remember XV over Ultimo Dragon, who pulls Francine into the champion's chair swing and later knocks Guerrera out with the belt; Francine breaks up the cover, lowblows Dragon and hits a DDT, and Guerrera hits a 450 Splash for the pin (B), receives the new belt from Jim Molineaux, and kisses Francine. On the Saturday show he beats The Great Sasuke with a Juvi Driver in the twelfth minute and, on Revolution on the first Monday of December, Eddie Guerrero with a Juvi Driver (B); the diary's next preview books him against Christopher Daniels.
note: The history lists the reign as 'present', and the pages through the first Saturday of December show the champion keeping the belt (the diary's own preview of November To Remember XV and its Saturday show call him a new champion, a week after the win on 26 November); no end date is filed, and the record of these pages ends with Guerrera still the champion.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
label: Paul Burchill

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Paul Burchill: 30 November 2007 - present" (in-game dates); the text agrees: November To Remember XV, PDF p.1721: "Your winner and NEW ECW World Heavyweight Champion... 'The New Franchise' Paul Burchill!"

how: Paul Burchill, entering behind Shane Douglas, Steven Regal, Vito and Kelly Thomaselli, pins Raven at November To Remember XV in the Loser Leaves ECW Match, in a contest with no interference allowed: Raven throws him from the crow's nest wall through two tables and hits the Raven Effect onto a chair, Burchill kicks out, hits a C-4 from the top rope and then a Shooting Star Press for the three, in a match the diary rates A*; Raven is out of ECW and Douglas raises the new champion's hand. Paul Heyman's Code of Diminishing Extremes, read on the Saturday show with Douglas, defends the title under modified British rules, twelve five-minute rounds on a two-out-of-three-falls basis with judges after an hour. Burchill beats CM Punk in a non-title match with a C-4 and a Moonsault after Sabu and The Sandman, 'ECW Enforcers', clear the Nest; on Revolution on the first Monday of December he and Vito Thomaselli beat Punk and Goliath by disqualification, Rhino gores him on that show and again on the Saturday show, where Rhino beats Vito in a number one contendership match and earns the title match at Masters of Pain.
note: The history lists the reign as 'present', and the record of these pages ends with Burchill still the champion and Rhino the number one contender for Masters of Pain.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
label: Ricky Marvin

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW International All Action Championship, listed as "Ricky Marvin: 30 November 2007 - present" (in-game dates); the text agrees: November To Remember XV, PDF p.1694: Marvin pins Slyk Tayshaun Dudley with a Shining Wizard, "it looks like we have our new International All Action Champion".

how: Ricky Marvin, the winner of the International All Action Title Tournament's semi-final over Excalibur, beats Slyk Tayshaun Dudley in the final at November To Remember XV: Slyk comes back in the fifth minute until Big Dick Jr. slides in and hits his cousin with a Total Penetration, and Marvin pins him with a Shining Wizard in a match the diary rates C-; he dances round the ring with the belt. The Code of Diminishing Extremes read on the Saturday show sets the title to lucha libre rules, a twenty count when a wrestler is outside the ring and victory on two falls out of three.
note: The history lists the reign as 'present', and the record of these pages ends with Marvin still the champion.

title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
label: Second Generation of Dudleyz (Slyk Tayshaun Dudley and Big Dick Dudley Jr.)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "Second Generation of Dudleys (Big Dick Dudley Jr. & Slyk Tayshaun Dudley): 4 November 2007 - present" (in-game dates); the text places the win on Revolution, Monday, week 1, December 2007, PDF p.1747: "...ECW Undisputed Tag Team Champions... how: Slyk Tayshaun Dudley and Big Dick Dudley Jr. win the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles on Revolution on the first Monday of December: the Dudley Boyz's defence against Thomaselli-Thomaselli '08 becomes a brawl when Slyk comes in with a baseball bat and Dick Jr. with a chair, referee Jim Molineaux rules a no contest and the match is restarted as a Three Way Dance, The Sandman canes Dick Jr. and slides Slyk in, Dick Jr. hits Brandon with a Total Penetration, Slyk breaks up Bubba Ray's pin and puts Bubba in the Boston Crabs, and Bubba taps (B-). The Saturday show's backstage scene has the new champions with Daizy Dudley planning to use the belts as leverage over their uncles to learn the family secret; they beat Thomaselli-Thomaselli '08 in their first defence, Brandon tapping to the Boston Crabs while Dick Jr. covers Sal, and the recap has them keep the belts over Christopher Daniels and Tajiri despite in-fighting.
note: The history dates the win 4 November 2007 and lists the reign as 'present'; the text places the win on the first Monday of December, after the Dudley Boyz's own win of the unified belts at November To Remember XV. The dates are the history's; the order of the shows is the text's.
